**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 92, verses 1–4:**

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Surah al-Layl** (The Night)

It is a Meccan surah, and its verses number twenty-one. The Prophet's ﷺ saying to Mu'adh was mentioned earlier: "Why did you not pray with *Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la*, *wa al-shamsi wa duhaha*, and *wa al-layli idha yaghsha*?"

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

﴿By the night when it covers﴾ ﴿and the day when it appears in brightness﴾ ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾ ﴿indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾

﴿By the night when it covers﴾: that is, it covers the sun or the day with its darkness, so that the light goes away. ﴿And the day when it appears in brightness﴾: that is, it shows itself when the night departs, or it becomes clear with the rising of the sun.

The Imam said: The verb of covering is expressed in the present tense (*mudari'*), because of the darkness that has come upon the original light, which is the most perfect of the manifestations of existence, to the extent that existence itself is expressed by it. As for the brightening of the day, it is a necessary consequence of this, and so it is expressed in the past tense (*madi*), as its explanation has already passed.

﴿And by Him who created the male and the female﴾: that is, and by the Powerful One who created the two kinds, male and female, of every species that reproduces. Here *ma* is a relative pronoun (*mawsula*) in the sense of *man* (who), and it was chosen to indicate the attributive sense, as was mentioned earlier.

The Imam said: He swore by His essence under this description only because it implies the attribute of knowledge that encompasses the finest details of matter and what is in it, and it points to the perfection of His craftsmanship. For it cannot be conceived that this difference between male and female in animals comes about by mere chance from a nature that has no awareness of what it does, as some deniers claim. The original components of matter are equally related to being male or being female, so the formation of offspring from the same elements, sometimes male and sometimes female, is evidence that the one who set up this order is knowing of what He does and firm in what He arranges and makes. End of quotation.

(Her) His words: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ are the response to the oath (*jawab al-qasam*). Or the response is implied, as its detail has already passed. That is: they differ in their recompense and separate in their outcome. Among them is that by which the striver is made happy, and among them is that by which he is made wretched, so how far apart these two are, as He explains afterwards. *Shatta* is either the plural of *shatit* or *shatt*, in the sense of scattered, and the verbal noun in the genitive construction indicates generality, so it is plural in meaning. For this reason it was described by *shatta*, which is plural. There is another view, that it is the singular verbal noun of a feminine form, like *dhikra* and *bushra*. In that case it is either given a supplied genitive noun, or it is treated as a figurative description, or its very essence is taken to be divergence, for emphasis.

Al-Razi said: Close to this are His words: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20], His words: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was a defiant sinner? They are not equal﴾ [al-Sajdah: 18], and His words: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them as those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is that which they judge﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 92, verse 5–11:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5–11] ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah),﴾ ﴿and affirms the best (reward),﴾ ﴿We will ease him toward ease.﴾ ﴿But as for him who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient,﴾ ﴿and denies the best (reward),﴾ ﴿We will ease him toward hardship.﴾ ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (into the pit).﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah)﴾ is a detailing of those divergent endeavours, and a clarification of their outcome, which has preceded.

(p-6176) Al-Razi said: In "gives" (a'ta) there are two possibilities:

The first: that what is meant is spending wealth in all the ways of good, such as freeing slaves, ransoming captives, and strengthening the Muslims against their enemy, as Abu Bakr used to do, whether that is obligatory or voluntary. This unrestricted usage is like His saying: ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3], for what is meant by it is everything that is spending in the way of Allah, whether obligatory or voluntary. Allah has praised a people, saying: ﴿And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [al-Insan: 8], and He said at the end of this surah: ﴿But the most fearing of Allah will be spared it,﴾ [al-Layl: 17] ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾ [al-Layl: 18], to the end of the verse.

The second: that His saying "gives" encompasses giving the rights of wealth and giving the rights of the self in obedience to Allah, the Exalted. It is said: "So-and-so gave obedience (al-ta'ah) and gave ease (al-si'ah)." End of quotation.

However, the first is the more fitting sense for "giving," because it is well known that it is connected specifically with wealth, and it has come in opposition to the mention of stinginess and wealth. ﴿And fears (Allah)﴾, i.e., fears his Lord and so avoids His prohibitions.

﴿And affirms the best (reward)﴾ [al-Layl: 6], i.e., affirms the good reward. Qatadah said: that is, he affirmed Allah's good promise. This has the same meaning as the statement of Mujahid: it is Paradise, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever commits a good deed, We will increase for him therein good﴾ [al-Shura: 23], so He called the multiplication of reward "good" (husna). Al-Qashani said: that is, he affirmed the excellent virtue which is the rank of perfection through knowledgeable faith, for if he were not certain of the existence of a perfect perfection, he would not be able to ascend.

﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾ [al-Layl: 7], i.e., We will prepare him and grant him success to the easy path, which is conducting oneself on the way of truth, because of the strength of his certainty.

Al-Shihab said: Since it leads to ease, which is the easy matter by which people find rest, it is described as "ease" (yusra), on the basis that it is a clear metaphor, or an unrestricted metonymy, or a figurative extension in the attribution.

﴿But as for him who withholds﴾ [al-Layl: 8], i.e., from spending in the way of Allah, and withholding what Allah has granted him of His bounty from being spent in the ways in which Allah has commanded it to be spent. ﴿And considers himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Layl: 8], i.e., regarding his Lord, so he does not desire Him through action, or through obedience to Him by increasing in what He has entrusted to him; or he considers himself self-sufficient by his wealth from acquiring virtue, and became blind thereby to the truth.

﴿And denies the best (reward)﴾ [al-Layl: 9], i.e., denies the existence of the reward of the good for those who believe in the truth, because he is self-sufficient with the worldly life and veiled by it from the world of the Hereafter.

﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 10], i.e., toward the difficult path that leads to everlasting wretchedness.

Al-Imam said: The difficult course (al-khutta al-'usra) is the course by which a person lowers himself, diminishes its rights, descends with it to the depths of animality, and plunges it into the mire of sin. It is the most difficult of the two courses for a human being, because he finds no helper in it, neither from his nature nor from people.

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (into the pit)﴾ [al-Layl: 11], i.e., what his wealth, for which he toiled in acquiring and spent his life in preserving and became insolent toward the truth on its account, will not benefit him when he perishes. It is from the saying: "He fell (taradda) from the mountain into the pit." In the use of this expression there is an indication that by what he has put forward of his wicked deeds, he is the one who destroys and casts himself down, and he is the one who digs his own grave with his own hoof. "Ma" here is either negating or interrogative in the sense of denial. And His saying:

That is: upon Us, in accordance with Our decree, which is founded on consummate wisdom, since We created creation for the reform of the earth, is that We make clear to them the path of guidance, so that they may avoid the places of ruin. Glory be to Him has done this by sending the Messengers, sending down the Books, and enabling them to reason and to seek insight, by creating the intellect and bestowing the power of choice.

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life).﴾ That is: (they belong to Us) in ownership and creation. Therefore your turning away from guidance does not harm Us. This is because of His absolute self-sufficiency, His sole ownership of what is in both abodes, and His being in the grip of His dominion, such that no one can stand between Him and it, nor can anyone obtain it, so that the non-guidance of anyone would harm Him or his guidance would benefit Him. This indicates the boundlessness of His greatness and the perfection of His dominance and majesty. Whoever is like this is worthy that one should hasten to obey Him and beware of disobeying Him; for this reason He follows it with His words: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire blazing.﴾ [al-Layl: 14] That is: it flares and blazes, and it is the Fire of the Hereafter.

﴿None will enter it except the most wretched,﴾ [al-Layl: 15] ﴿Who denied﴾ [al-Layl: 16] That is: the truth that came to him, ﴿and turned away﴾ [al-Layl: 16] That is: from the signs of his Lord and its proofs, whose matter He has made clear and whose light has dazzled, out of obstinacy and disbelief.

﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it,﴾ [al-Layl: 17] ﴿Who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾ [al-Layl: 18] That is: he spends his wealth in the way of good, purifying himself from the filth of stinginess and the defilement of withholding.

﴿And for whom there is no favor (owed) to anyone that must be repaid,﴾ [al-Layl: 19] That is: no hand that he must reward for it; that is, he does not give for the sake of recompense or reciprocity.

﴿Except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ [al-Layl: 20] That is: rather, he gives seeking the Face of his Lord and desiring His good pleasure, not for any other purpose of recompense, praise, or reputation. How could it not be so, when wealth is the foundation of actions, the raising of the structures of right guidance, and the demolition of the palaces of corruption?

As for His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And he is going to be well-pleased.﴾ [al-Layl: 21] Ibn Jarir said: That is, this one who gives his wealth in the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will indeed be well-pleased, purifying himself with what Allah will reward him in the Hereafter in return for what he gave in this world in His way, when he meets his Lord, blessed and exalted is He. In this there is a generous promise of attaining everything he seeks in the most perfect and beautiful manner, since through it contentment is realized. This is on the understanding that the pronoun in "yarda" (he is pleased) refers to "al-atqa" (the most righteous), not to the Lord. Al-Shihab said: This is the most suitable reading for the context and for the coherence of the pronouns.

Then he said: The expression "sawfa" (surely/soon) is used to convey that pleasure requires great expenditure, and a little wealth is not sufficient for the servant to reach the degree of Divine pleasure.

Admonition:

Ibn Kathir said: More than one of the exegetes mentioned that these verses were revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), to the extent that some of them reported an ijma' (scholarly consensus, a binding agreement of qualified scholars) among the exegetes on this. There is no doubt that he is included in them, and that he is the most worthy of the Ummah of their general application; for the wording is general, namely His words: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it,﴾ [al-Layl: 17] ﴿Who gives his wealth to purify himself,﴾ [al-Layl: 18] ﴿And for whom there is no favor (owed) to anyone that must be repaid.﴾ [al-Layl: 19]

However, he is the foremost of the Ummah and its precursor in all these attributes and in the rest of the praiseworthy attributes. He was a truthful one (siddiq), pious, generous, and bountiful, spending his wealth in obedience to his Master and in support of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). How many dirhams and dinars he spent seeking the Face of his Generous Lord! No one among the people had a favor with him that he needed to repay, but rather his bounty and kindness were toward the chiefs and leaders of the various tribes. For this reason, 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud, who was the chief of Thaqif, said to him on the day of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya: "By Allah! Were it not for a hand you have over me, I would not have repaid you for it, I would have answered you." Al-Siddiq had spoken harshly to him in speech. If this was his condition with the chiefs of the Arabs and the leaders of the tribes, then what of those other than them?

In the two Sahihs it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends a pair in the way of Allah will be called by the keepers of Paradise: 'O servant of Allah, this is good.'" Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah! There is no need for whoever is called from it, so is anyone called from all of them?" He said: "Yes, and I hope that you will be among them." End.

(p-6179) Some scholars went to the second view, among them al-Imam, who said: That is, "and He will indeed be well-pleased with that most righteous one who seeks, with the attribute of His pleasure." Then he said: The expression "sawfa" (surely/soon) is used to convey that pleasure requires great expenditure, and a little wealth is not sufficient for the servant to reach the degree of Divine pleasure.

Admonition:

Ibn Kathir said: More than one of the exegetes mentioned that these verses were revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), to the extent that some of them reported an ijma' (scholarly consensus, a binding agreement of qualified scholars) among the exegetes on this. There is no doubt that he is included in them, and that he is the most worthy of the Ummah of their general application; for the wording is general, namely His words: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it,﴾ [al-Layl: 17] ﴿Who gives his wealth to purify himself,﴾ [al-Layl: 18] ﴿And for whom there is no favor (owed) to anyone that must be repaid.﴾ [al-Layl: 19]

However, he is the foremost of the Ummah and its precursor in all these attributes and in the rest of the praiseworthy attributes. He was a truthful one (siddiq), pious, generous, and bountiful, spending his wealth in obedience to his Master and in support of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). How many dirhams and dinars he spent seeking the Face of his Generous Lord! No one among the people had a favor with him that he needed to repay, but rather his bounty and kindness were toward the chiefs and leaders of the various tribes. For this reason, 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud, who was the chief of Thaqif, said to him on the day of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya: "By Allah! Were it not for a hand you have over me, I would not have repaid you for it, I would have answered you." Al-Siddiq had spoken harshly to him in speech. If this was his condition with the chiefs of the Arabs and the leaders of the tribes, then what of those other than them?

In the two Sahihs it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends a pair in the way of Allah will be called by the keepers of Paradise: 'O servant of Allah, this is good.'" Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah! There is no need for whoever is called from it, so is anyone called from all of them?" He said: "Yes, and I hope that you will be among them." End.
